ios.desc:
Welcome to Fog. The minimalist notes app designed to eliminate organizing friction while keeping you in complete control.

Just open the app and write. Fog uses smart, on-device intelligence to propose titles, summarize your folders, and surface what you need, without ever changing anything behind your back.

KEY FEATURES

* Smart Title Suggestions: Start typing immediately. Fog reads your context and proposes a title so you never stare at "Untitled." Keep it, edit it, or tap for another.
* Folders Your Way: Select your notes and group them; Fog automatically names the folder and writes a summary of what's inside. Or build your own from scratch.
* Ask Your Notes: Traditional search coming up short? Ask Fog directly. On-device AI scans your notes and answers your questions in plain English.
* System-Wide Spotlight Search: Instantly locate notes across your device by their text, title, or smart background tags.
* Siri AI: Powered by Apple Intelligence, Fog taps into the latest App Intent domains to let you interact with your notes naturally using Siri.

PRIVACY FIRST & FULLY OFFLINE

* 100% On-Device Intelligence: Powered by Apple’s Foundation Models. Fast, local, and works with zero latency, even completely offline or on a plane.
* Zero Third-Party Servers: Your thoughts stay in your ecosystem. Stored locally with SwiftData and synced seamlessly across your devices via personal iCloud.
* Universal Compatibility: Enjoy a fast, clean note-taking experience on any device, with automated AI features available on supported Apple Intelligence hardware.

WHY FOG?

* The best notes app is the one that gets out of your way. Fog removes the heavy lifting of filing, naming, and summarizing so you can stay in your flow.

Stop fighting your note app. Download Fog and keep your focus where it belongs.

quotes.text:
Hey everyone,

This is my first time posting on Show HN, so hello there.

Back in March, I launched my first app on the App Store. It was a notes app that uses Apple's on-device foundation model to organize your notes for you, and I called it Fog. And boy did I learn a lot. Looking at the notes app category and how saturated it currently is, I wanted to try something different. Privacy is #1, so notes should stay on the device, keeping the user in control. Then there was the AI aspect I was using to "automatically organize". So when a user creates a new note, it auto-names the note, generates tags, and tries to do a similarity search against existing folders with the same tags, and in the end the note would land in the folder, all autonomously. Sounds cool in theory and, from my understanding, no other app really did this, in addition to all AI processing happening on device using the same model that powers Apple Intelligence and Siri (works offline too). But this backfired b/c even I started using it less and less b/c I kept forgetting "what was that note called?" "Where'd it go?" "Why'd it move?". Notes and folders were ever-changing, which I also thought was cool but maybe not practical for what a note is meant to be: something to reference.
